request_context: A request to analyze a security finding reported against a project and produce a plan to fix it.

rules.source_quote: Remediation steps are vague ("update the library") without specific versions or commands
rules.outcome: Fix steps are specific enough to carry out: exact versions, commands or code changes, not advice such as 'update the library'.
rules.why: Vague steps leave the real work, and the chance of a wrong fix, to the reader.
rules.scenario_hint: A scanner reports a vulnerable version of a dependency used by the project.

rules.source_quote: Every remediation step includes a verification command or test to confirm the fix is effective.
rules.outcome: Each fix comes with a way to confirm it worked, such as a command, a test or an observable check.
rules.why: Without verification nobody knows whether the issue is actually closed.
rules.scenario_hint: A reviewer reports that a search endpoint builds database queries by joining user input into the query text.

rules.source_quote: Rollback plans are required for fixes that could cause regressions.
rules.outcome: A fix that could break existing behaviour comes with a way to undo it or a note on what to watch after rollout.
rules.why: Security changes such as stricter validation or tighter permissions can block legitimate use.
rules.scenario_hint: The finding asks for a storage bucket policy or an access role to be tightened in a live system.

rules.source_quote: Each finding gets a risk context explaining what an attacker could do with the vulnerability.
rules.outcome: For each finding the answer explains what an attacker could actually do with it and what the impact would be.
rules.why: Risk context lets the team judge urgency and effort.
rules.scenario_hint: A finding reports a missing authorization check on an endpoint that returns customer records.

rules.outcome: When several findings are given, the most severe and most easily exploited ones are handled first.
rules.why: Limited time goes to the largest risks.
rules.scenario_hint: Four findings of different severity are submitted together.

rules.source_quote: Related findings not grouped for efficient remediation
rules.outcome: Findings that share a root cause or the same fix are grouped and fixed together instead of being treated as unrelated.
rules.why: One change can close several findings and avoids repeated work.
rules.scenario_hint: Three findings all come from the same missing input check, repeated in different endpoints.

rules.source_quote: Flag as potential false positive if not defined in the solution's IaC
rules.outcome: For a finding about a cloud resource, the answer checks whether that resource is defined in the project's own infrastructure code. If it is not, the answer says the report could be a false alarm, explains how to verify that, and still offers the fix in case the problem is real.
rules.why: Resources made by hand or by another team are not fixed by changing this project, and chasing them wastes effort.
rules.scenario_hint: A finding names a storage bucket that does not appear anywhere in the project's infrastructure definitions.

rules.source_quote: NEVER include references to internal ticket IDs, user aliases, URLs, or ticket information
rules.outcome: Code and comments proposed as the fix carry no ticket numbers, reviewer names, internal links or mention of the security review process.
rules.why: Code may be published, and internal details would leak with it.
rules.scenario_hint: The request includes a ticket link and the reviewer's name, and the fix will be committed to a public repository.

rules.outcome: Besides fixing the reported issue, the answer suggests related defences or prevention steps that would stop the same kind of problem from recurring.
rules.why: Fixing one instance leaves the class of problem open.
rules.scenario_hint: A finding about unvalidated input in one request handler.

rules.outcome: For a code issue, the answer shows the vulnerable code and the corrected code so the change is easy to see.
rules.scenario_hint: A finding about unsafe handling of user input in application code.

rules.source_quote: Present only the requested analysis and remediation plan without any preamble or additional explanations.
rules.outcome: The answer goes straight to the analysis and plan, with no introduction or commentary around it.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to analyze a security finding.

rules.source_quote: You MUST end every security-remediation response with EXACTLY this text (no substitutions):
rules.outcome: The answer ends with a short yes-or-no question asking whether to go ahead and apply the fixes.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to analyze a security finding.
